title: Interleave-aware slot allocator and kernel-hinting for multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: At production scale we see recurring tail-latency spikes and bandwidth contention during prefill->decode handoffs on multi-GPU hosts. Root causes include suboptimal kernel choices for attention windows, poorly aligned microbatch handovers across tensor/pipeline parallel stages, and NCCL bursts that create short-term congestion. This ticket designs and implements an interleave-aware slot allocator that coordinates handoffs across stages and surfaces lightweight kernel-hinting to the runtime kernel selector to reduce handoff jitter and NCCL overlap impact.
proposal: Introduce a slot allocator that assigns 'handoff windows' for prefill and decode segments per-device, driven by an interleave map derived from request sequence-length distribution and active microbatch footprint. The allocator will produce: 1) soft start offsets for prefill microbatches to avoid synchronized NCCL all-reduces, and 2) kernel-hints (attention tile sizes, fused-softmax preference, quantized-kernel preference) pushed to the kernel selector before prefill begins. Combine this with a light-weight backpressure token to defer low-priority prefill traffic when NCCL bandwidth saturation is detected.
design_notes:
- Interleave map computed from rolling telemetry (per-model, per-route): sequence length histogram, active microbatches, KV cache reuse ratio.
- Slot allocator outputs per-GPU window offset (ms), preferred microbatch size, and kernel-hint tag (one of: AUTO, ATTEN_TILE_64, ATTEN_TILE_128, FUSED_SOFTMAX, QUANT_FAST).
- Kernel selector receives hint and remains free to override based on hardware capabilities; hints bias heuristic scoring.
- NCCL smoothing: implement randomized jitter within a bounded offset to avoid worst-case alignment.
- Rollout uses model-level feature flag and route opt-in; default off for critical customers.
- Keep changes minimal in hot-path: allocator runs in scheduling plane (non-hot), kernel-hint is a small metadata field in request envelope.
- Integrate with existing batching and KV prefetch subsystems to avoid duplicated prefix caching work.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: reduces worst-case synchronized NCCL bursts, lowers p95 tail, provides a predictable knob for kernel selection.
- Cons: added scheduling complexity and additional metadata overhead; mis-tuned offsets can increase median latency for small requests.
- Mitigation: conservative defaults + automatic rollback when tail worsens by >5% over baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end latency test shows >=10% reduction in p95 for mixed prefill/decode synthetic workload with 90/10 long/short sequences. 2) Bandwidth telemetry shows reduced burstiness of NCCL allreduce events. 3) No regression in median latency for <32-token requests. 4) Feature can be toggled per-model and rolled back safely.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator logic and kernel-hint serialization.
- Local multi-GPU integration tests (4x A100) exercising staggered microbatches.
- Perf harness: replay production trace (sanitized) for 24 hours in staging and compare p50/p95/p99.
- Chaos test: inject synthetic NCCL bandwidth delays to validate backpressure behavior.
- Canary rollout: start with 1% of traffic on runtime-1.20 cluster, monitor 48h, increase if stable.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature flag gated by model. 2) Internal alpha: enable on internal-bench model and run 72h smoke. 3) Canary 1% for non-SLA customers. 4) Expand to 25% after 48h stability. 5) Full rollout across runtime-1.20 if metrics meet acceptance criteria. 6) Add automatic rollback threshold in console with alerting.
observability_and_dashboards: Create new dashboard tiles: 'Interleave allocator: offset distribution', 'Kernel-hint adoption by model', 'NCCL burst index vs cluster load', and add regression alert for p95 increase >5% over baseline. Link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtime/prefill-interleave-290721
notes_for_reviewer: Focus review on kernel-hint API surface and guarantees about backward compatibility. Check that hint scoring in kernel selector is additive and doesn't hard-fail on unknown tags. Verify that allocator failure modes (OOM, telemetry gaps) gracefully fall back to current behavior.
